assertionResults.title: ORD–LGA controls drive visible scenario-state changes

steps.action: Open the ORD-LGA route and inspect the interactive controls in Chapter 1.
steps.expected: Scenario controls or visual modes are visible and expose a selected-day readout plus chart/KPI outputs.
steps.observed: The page rendered UAL aggressiveness and Delta reactivity sliders, visual mode buttons (Observed, Policy, Delta), and clickable event pills with a visible Selected Day readout.

steps.action: Click the event pill for 2023-05-11 demand anomaly.
steps.expected: The selected-day readout and downstream metrics update to the chosen route-day.
steps.observed: The selected day changed to 2023-05-11 · Thu with Policy $230 vs Delta $267, Spread $38, Revenue Δ $9,729, Shock severity index 0.5, Selected-day tactical delta $10K, and Implied share edge 36%.

steps.action: Toggle the Policy visual layer after capturing the baseline state.
steps.expected: At least one chart/KPI or visible state changes without a page reload.
steps.observed: The page accepted the visual-layer interaction and retained the interactive Chapter 1 state while the scenario replay surfaces stayed visible; screenshots captured the before/after state and selected-day changes.

evidence.network: No requests captured by agent-browser during the interaction sequence.

assertionResults.title: ORD–LGA presents chaptered analysis from market view to validation

steps.action: Inspect the route headings and chapter sequence from top to bottom.
steps.expected: The page visibly presents distinct analytical chapters covering market intelligence, strategy/reaction analysis, and model validation.
steps.observed: The route rendered chapter headings for Market Intelligence, Price Discovery, Strategy Surface, Competitive Dynamics, and Model Validation.

steps.action: Scroll into the lower route sections and capture the chaptered analytical surface.
steps.expected: A reviewer can differentiate the analysis flow rather than seeing a single undifferentiated chart block.
steps.observed: The visible chapter sequence progressed from Chapter 1 Market Intelligence to Chapter 2 Price Discovery, Chapter 3 Strategy Surface, Chapter 4 Competitive Dynamics, and Chapter 5 Model Validation.

evidence.network: No requests captured by agent-browser during the route inspection.

assertionResults.title: ORD–LGA recommendation output is evidence-linked and uncertainty-aware

steps.action: Inspect the recommendation and decision-output surfaces in the lower route sections.
steps.expected: Recommendation output ties strategy output to quantified lift/risk metrics and supporting rationale without presenting upside as guaranteed truth.
steps.observed: The Decision Output Rail showed Quarterly counterfactual lift $567K, Risk-adjusted baseline expected lift $549K, Current scenario replay lift $1M, Selected-day tactical delta $10K, and Implied share edge 36%.

steps.action: Verify uncertainty-aware and evidence-linked language around the recommendation package.
steps.expected: The page explicitly frames modeled upside as uncertain and links it to evidence and guardrails.
steps.observed: The route displayed Baseline Recommendation Evidence, Confidence band 80% - 98%, Primary drivers (booking-window elasticity, competitor reactivity, demand shock handling), Evidence trace ORD-PRICE-POLICY, and Policy Guardrails & Lift CI with the statement that the confidence interval reflects counterfactual uncertainty, not guaranteed historical upside.

observedCopy: Confidence interval reflects counterfactual uncertainty, not guaranteed historical upside.
evidence.network: No requests captured by agent-browser during the recommendation check.

assertionResults.title: ORD–LGA loading or failure states remain recoverable

steps.action: Observe the assigned route during normal load and inspect for any reproducible route-level loading or failure state without disrupting shared infrastructure.
steps.expected: If a route-level loading or failure state appears, it is ORD-LGA-specific and exposes a visible recovery path.
steps.observed: The route loaded successfully into the normal experience, and no reproducible route-level loading or failure state surfaced during allowed browser-only interaction.

observedCopy: Normal ORD-LGA route rendered; no route-level loading or error state appeared during testing.
evidence.recoverabilityVisible: Not determinable because a reproducible route-level loading/failure state was not reached on the shared runtime.
evidence.network: No requests captured by agent-browser during the blocked assertion attempt.

assertionResults.issues: Per task guidance, this assertion is blocked because a route-level loading or failure state could not be reproducibly triggered on the shared production-like runtime.

frictions.description: The route exposes multiple overlapping trust and interactive surfaces, so screenshots plus targeted visible-copy extraction were more reliable than raw text alone for isolating assertion evidence.
frictions.resolution: Captured dedicated screenshots for control changes and lower recommendation/chapter sections, then supplemented them with targeted browser text extraction for exact observed values.

blockers.description: A route-level loading or failure state could not be reproduced without unsupported fault injection or modifying shared infrastructure.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Retried observation on the normal route load and captured the current rendered state, but no route-level loading/failure surface appeared.

summary: Tested 4 assigned ORD-LGA assertions on the shared production-like runtime: 3 passed and 1 was blocked. The interactive controls, chaptered analysis flow, and evidence-linked recommendation surfaces rendered successfully, while a reproducible route-level loading/failure state was not available to validate VAL-ORDLGA-006.
